summary_paragraph: Mr. Thompson was admitted after his implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (ICD) delivered four shocks during a family event while dancing. He remained asymptomatic with no chest pain, syncope, or heart failure symptoms. Evaluation revealed no acute cardiac injury, and device interrogation showed inappropriate therapy due to sinus tachycardia misclassified as ventricular tachycardia, triggered by ventricular ectopy. The ICD was reprogrammed to raise the threshold for therapy from 150 to 190 bpm, and his metoprolol dose was increased to reduce exercise-induced tachycardia. His chronic conditions, including systolic and diastolic heart failure, coronary artery disease, mechanical aortic valve on anticoagulation, cirrhosis, and COPD, remained stable. He was discharged home with follow-up in the device clinic and instructions to monitor blood pressure with the new medication dose.
problems: Mechanical complication of automatic implantable cardiac defibrillator
Chronic combined systolic and diastolic heart failure
Coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery
Diabetes mellitus without mention of complication, type II or unspecified type, not stated as uncontrolled
Heart valve replaced by other means
Cirrhosis of liver without mention of alcohol
Chronic airway obstruction, not elsewhere classified
Personal history of transient ischemic attack (TIA), and cerebral infarction without residual deficits
Surgical operation with implant of artificial internal device causing abnormal patient reaction, or later complication,without mention of misadventure at time of operation
